top_story_title: Barracuda Email Security Gateway: pre-auth chain to remote root, with the full chain now public
top_story_summary: watchTowr Labs published a two-flaw chain against Barracuda's Email Security Gateway (ESG) that ends in command execution as root with no login at all. The reporting names CVE-2026-116606 as an authorization bypass an unauthenticated attacker can reach directly, chained with CVE-2026-111560. Barracuda released patches on the Monday before disclosure; watchTowr published the technical write-up on the Thursday. Neither source states a fixed build number, so confirm the fixed release against Barracuda's own advisory before you schedule anything.
top_actions: Identify every Barracuda ESG appliance (physical, virtual and hosted) and confirm in the appliance UI which build is actually installed - do not assume an update channel has applied the fix.
Apply Barracuda's patched release; check the vendor advisory for the fixed release, as the public reporting does not state a build number.
Rotate everything the appliance holds after patching: admin credentials, API tokens, LDAP/AD bind accounts, SMTP relay credentials and TLS certificates - a pre-patch compromise survives the upgrade.
Restrict the ESG administrative interface to a management VLAN or jump host and remove it from internet exposure entirely; SMTP exposure is unavoidable, the admin plane is not.
Hunt for compromise: unexpected local accounts, new or modified scripts and web resources, outbound connections from the appliance to unfamiliar hosts, and configuration restores you did not perform.
executive_summary: **Barracuda ESG** - a public chain of CVE-2026-116606 and CVE-2026-111560 gives unauthenticated remote root on the Email Security Gateway; patches are out, exploitation is not reported yet. Patch on an emergency change.

**Cisco** - the October Node.js/Brotli bundle advisory includes CVE-2026-111497, which is on the CISA KEV catalog with a BOD 26-04 due date of 2026-11-10. Four days out, and the affected-product list is in the advisory, not in the feed.
**D-Link** - multiple zero-days in DGS-3130 series managed switches have mitigations but no patch. Treat these as permanently exposed until D-Link says otherwise.

**Cisco IOS XE** - SANS honeypots are logging exploit attempts consistent with CVE-2023-20198 (KEV, 2023). Three years on, the Web UI is still being swept. Check for privilege-15 accounts you did not create.

**Cisco / certificate trust** - emergency distrust of eMudhra root and intermediate CAs after eight intermediate private keys proved brute-forceable in seconds. Audit anything on your network that trusts them.

**OpenSSH** - CVE-2026-123158 is being exploited within hours of disclosure: a password-auth bypass on musl-based Linux with PAM disabled, fixed in 10.6p2. Ask your appliance vendors whether their firmware is in scope.
**AI** - Check Point Research documents ARTEX, an autonomous AI pentest platform in criminal use with 1,608 live public instances. Plan patch windows for internet-facing devices in days.
key_actions: **Barracuda** — Inventory all ESG appliances - physical, virtual and hosted - and read the installed build from the appliance UI rather than trusting an update channel.
**Barracuda** — Apply the patched release Barracuda has published; check the vendor advisory for the fixed release and record the build you land on.
**Cisco** — Pull the affected-product list from the Cisco advisory and match it against your asset inventory by model and running version - the feed entry does not name products.
**Cisco** — Apply the Cisco fixed releases where published; check the vendor advisory for the fixed release and re-check it, as Cisco states the advisory will be updated.
**D-Link** — Apply D-Link's published mitigation measures exactly as written, then verify them on each unit rather than assuming the template took.

**D-Link** — Restrict the management plane now: management ACLs permitting only your management subnet, out-of-band management where you have it, and no management reachability from user or guest VLANs.
**Barracuda** — Confirm the patch Barracuda released is actually installed on every ESG appliance, and note the date it landed relative to the public disclosure.
**Barracuda** — If the appliance was unpatched after the disclosure date, treat it as potentially compromised: rotate credentials, tokens and certificates, and hunt before you close the ticket.

ai_defenses.solution: Firewall policy enforcement at network boundaries for AI agent traffic (no product named in the source)
ai_defenses.what_it_does: Cisco describes using firewalls as the point where AI agent activity becomes visible: revealing what agents reach, enforcing policy at network boundaries, and helping contain the risks of autonomous action. The post names no product, version or availability date.

headlines.title: Barracuda Networks is your new best friend (Barracuda Email Security Gateway Pre-Auth Remote Root RCE CVE-2026-116606 / CVE-2026-111560)
headlines.summary: watchTowr published a chain of two Barracuda Email Security Gateway flaws that gives an unauthenticated attacker remote root on the appliance.

headlines.title: Vulnerabilities in Node.js and Brotli Affecting Cisco Products: October 2026
headlines.summary: Cisco's October bundle advisory covers four High-severity Node.js and Brotli flaws, including KEV-listed CVE-2026-111497, in products that embed Node.js 22.x, 24.x or 26.x.

headlines.title: D-Link warns of multiple zero-days in DGS-3130 Series switches
headlines.summary: D-Link published mitigation measures, not patches, for multiple zero-day flaws in DGS-3130 series managed stackable switches.

headlines.title: Experts Demonstrate Barracuda Email Security Gateway Chain Enabling Root Access Without Login
headlines.summary: Reporting on the Barracuda ESG chain confirms CVE-2026-116606 is an authorization bypass usable with no login, with patches released on the Monday before disclosure.

headlines.title: Vulnerability Scans for Older Cisco IOS Vulnerability / Opt-Out Headers, (Thu, Nov 5th)
headlines.summary: SANS honeypots are logging exploit attempts against the Cisco IOS XE Web UI consistent with CVE-2023-20198, a KEV flaw from 2023.

headlines.title: Cisco Informational for Emergency Distrust of eMudhra Root and Intermediate Certificate Authorities
headlines.summary: Cisco issued an emergency-distrust notice for eMudhra root and intermediate CAs after researchers showed eight intermediate private keys can be brute-forced in seconds.
